# Story 27 — Manually reassign a ticket

---

## Prerequisites

- **Story 26 (in-app notifications for ticket events) must land first.** This story reuses that story's `createTicketNotification(...)` helper and extends its `NotificationType` union with a new `"ticket_reassigned"` value. See `.squad/plans/ticket-management/26-story-in-app-notifications-for-ticket-events.md`. If Story 26 has not landed when picking this up, **stop and finish Story 26 first** — do not re-implement notifications inline.
- Story 21 (agent availability toggle) has already introduced `isOnline` on `User`; this story reads it but does not modify it.
- Coordinate with any concurrent work on `ticket.routes.ts`'s `PATCH /:id` (category/priority edits) — this story adds a third field to the same endpoint, not a new one.

---

## Story Goal

Give admins, sub-admins, and reassign-permitted agents a working way to manually change a ticket's `assignedAgent` — from both the staff ticket queue (`/tickets`) and the ticket detail page (`/tickets/[id]`) — replacing the current disabled "Coming soon" `Repeat`-icon stub in `StaffTicketQueue.tsx`. Both surfaces use one server action calling one backend endpoint. Reassignments notify the previous and new assignee, and log who did what at `console.info` level.

**In scope:** tickets only. **Not in scope:** live-chat/conversation reassignment (deferred), full audit-trail UI (Story 13), escalation (Story 12), bulk reassignment.

Availability rule:
- **admin** and **sub-admin holding `tickets:reassign`** → may reassign to any active agent, online or not.
- **plain agent holding `tickets:reassign`** → may only reassign to an agent currently `isOnline: true`.
- Every caller may also choose "Unassigned" to clear the assignment (no online check applies).

## Product rules (from story)

**Current behaviour**
- The `Repeat` icon in `StaffTicketQueue.tsx` is disabled with a "Coming soon" title; clicking it does nothing.
- No frontend surface can change `assignedAgent` after auto-assignment.
- `PATCH /tickets/:id` accepts only `category` and `priority`.
- The queue's "Assigned to" cell is plain text; no link even for admins.

**New behaviour**
- Same icon becomes a live dropdown of assignable agents (plus "Unassigned"). Selecting an agent triggers reassignment.
- `TicketDetailSidebar` gains an "Assigned agent" `Select` mirroring category/priority.
- `PATCH /tickets/:id` accepts an optional nullable `assignedAgent` (ObjectId string or `null`).
- New `GET /tickets/assignable-agents` endpoint returns `{ id, name, isOnline }[]` — sorted by name — of every active, non-deleted agent, regardless of online status. Frontend uses `isOnline` only for client-side disabling when the viewer is a plain agent (per availability rule).
- Reassignment writes a `console.info` line: `"[ticket-reassigned] ticket=<id> from=<oldAgentId|null> to=<newAgentId|null> by=<callerId> at=<iso>"`.
- Previous assignee (if any and different from new) and new assignee (if any) receive an in-app notification via `createTicketNotification` with type `"ticket_reassigned"`.
- Queue's "Assigned to" agent name becomes a `Link` to `/admin/users/[id]/edit` only when the viewer is admin or holds `staff:view_account`; otherwise plain text (unchanged).

### 2 — New endpoint: `GET /tickets/assignable-agents`

**File:** `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts`

Register this route **before** `router.get("/:id", …)` (**~line 357**). Otherwise Express matches `assignable-agents` as an `:id`.

```ts
// Story 27: dropdown data source for manual reassignment. Deliberately NOT
// restricted to isOnline agents — the whole point of a manual reassign is
// handling an offline/overloaded agent. The frontend applies the
// online-only restriction for plain-agent callers (admin/subadmin unrestricted).
router.get(
  "/assignable-agents",
  requireAuth,
  requirePermission("tickets:reassign"),
  async (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
    const agents = await User.find({
      role: "agent",
      isActive: true,
      isDeleted: { $ne: true },
    })
      .select("_id name isOnline")
      .sort({ name: 1 })
      .lean();

    res.json({
      agents: agents.map((a) => ({
        id: String(a._id),
        name: a.name,
        isOnline: Boolean(a.isOnline),
      })),
    });
  },
);
```

---

### 3 — Extend `PATCH /tickets/:id` with reassignment

**File:** `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` (handler at **~line 395**)

Add `assignedAgent` handling alongside the existing `category` / `priority` branches:

- Use `"assignedAgent" in req.body` — same pattern the existing two fields use — to decide whether the field is being edited (distinguishes "unchanged" from `null` = unassign).
- Require the caller to have `tickets:reassign` **or** be `role === "admin"`; return `403` otherwise. Match the shape of the existing per-field permission check for category/priority.
- Enforce the availability rule:
  - If `req.user.role === "admin"` or `req.user.role === "subadmin"` → skip the online-check.
  - Otherwise (plain agent) → if `assignedAgent !== null`, load the target user with `.select("role isActive isDeleted isOnline")` and reject with `400` (message `"agent_not_online"`) unless `isOnline === true`. Always reject with `400` if the target is not `role: "agent"`, not active, or deleted.
- Load the previous `assignedAgent` id **before** the write.
- Perform the update in the same document-save flow the existing category/priority edits use so a single save persists all three fields at once.
- Emit `console.info("[ticket-reassigned] ticket=%s from=%s to=%s by=%s at=%s", ticketId, String(prev ?? null), String(next ?? null), req.user!.id, new Date().toISOString());`.
- Notifications (see task 4).

### 4 — Notifications: extend `NotificationType` and call the helper

**Files:**
- Wherever Story 26 defines `NotificationType` — extend the union with `"ticket_reassigned"`.
- The reassignment branch in `PATCH /tickets/:id`.

Call `createTicketNotification` twice on success:

- If `prev` exists **and** `prev !== next` → notify `prev` with type `"ticket_reassigned"` and payload identifying the ticket + the new assignee (or "unassigned"). The message text lives in the notification helper / i18n bag, not in the route.
- If `next` exists **and** `next !== prev` → notify `next` with type `"ticket_reassigned"` and payload identifying the ticket + who assigned it.

Do **not** await the notification calls in a way that blocks the response — match Story 26's pattern (fire-and-forget or `Promise.allSettled` with error logging), whichever Story 26 established.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Self-reassign (agent to themself):** Allowed; the reassign action still runs but `prev === next` → no notification fired. Enforced by the `prev !== next` guard in task 4.
- **Reassign to the same current assignee via the dropdown:** Same as above — no-op notification-wise; the PATCH still succeeds with `200`. Do not treat as an error.
- **Target agent flips `isActive: false` between dropdown load and click (plain-agent caller):** Backend re-validates and returns `400 agent_not_active`; frontend shows `reassignError` toast. Enforced in task 3.
- **Target agent goes offline between dropdown load and click (plain-agent caller):** Backend re-validates `isOnline` at save time. Returns `400 agent_not_online`. Enforced in task 3.
- **Non-existent target id (tampered client):** Zod validates ObjectId shape; the `User.findById` returns `null` → `400 target_not_found`.
- **Concurrent PATCHes racing on category + reassignment:** Both fields go through the same document save; Mongoose's last-write-wins is acceptable for this story (Story 13 will layer optimistic concurrency).
- **Story 26 not merged yet:** Do not implement notifications inline. Halt implementation with a `TODO: depends on Story 26` and coordinate. Enforced by the Prerequisites section.
- **Notification helper throws:** Ticket save must have already succeeded; notification failures are logged and swallowed (fire-and-forget, per Story 26's pattern). Endpoint still returns `200`.
- **Very long agent list (100+ agents):** Menu becomes a scrollable region; use `DropdownMenu`'s `max-h` + `overflow-auto` (see how `/admin/users` handles long lists). Not paginated in this story.
- **RTL:** Icon direction / dropdown alignment must respect `dir="rtl"`; use logical classes (`ms-`, `me-`) as done in `StaffTicketQueue.tsx` today.
- **Deactivated caller:** `requireAuth` already rejects; permission short-circuits do **not** bypass the `isActive` check (see `feedback_permission_gating_audit`). Double-check the new `requirePermission("tickets:reassign")` on `/assignable-agents` uses the standard middleware, not a role-only shortcut.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No schema migration.** `assignedAgent` already exists on `Ticket` with default `null` (`backend/src/models/Ticket.ts:42`).
- **API additive-only.** `updateTicketBodySchema`'s new field is optional; existing clients keep working.
- **Rollback:** Revert the PATCH branch, the new endpoint, and the frontend surfaces. The `Repeat` stub returns to its "Coming soon" state. No data cleanup needed — any reassignments already made stay valid (they are just `assignedAgent` changes the model has always supported).
- **Half-applied state (backend deployed, frontend not):** Manual API calls could reassign, but no UI to trigger them; safe.
- **Half-applied state (frontend deployed, backend not):** Dropdown shows a network error toast; no ticket state changes; safe.
